releases.name: strangerDanger v0.2.0
releases.body:
# strangerDanger v0.2.0

Secret and PII redaction guard for AI coding agents — now enforcing at the
OpenCode V2 request boundaries.

> **strangerDanger does not guarantee prevention of every secret leak.** It
> protects the specific surfaces listed below and fails closed everywhere else.
> Read the [limitations](#known-limitations) before relying on it.

## Features

- **Boundary redaction, not just auditing.** Registers all four V2 model-request
  hooks — `session.prompt`, `session.context`, `session.generate`,
  `session.title` — plus `session.compaction` and `tool.execute.after`, so
  prompts, tool results, transient generations, titles, and compaction
  transcripts are scanned immediately before transmission. Redaction is
  ordering-independent: whatever path a request takes, its assembled
  `system`/`messages` are re-scanned before dispatch.
- **236 detection rules** — 221 vendored from gitleaks (MIT), 12 clean-room
  additions for AI/ML providers, and 3 entropy detectors.
- **Standalone CLI** (`sd`): `scan`, `redact`, `audit`, `rules`, `allowlist`,
  `version`.
- **Five plugin tools**: `sd_status`, `sd_audit`, `sd_allowlist_add`,
  `sd_allowlist_show`, `sd_scan`.
- **Allowlist** by fingerprint, rule ID, path, or regex
  (`.strangerdanger-allowlist.toml`).
- **Independent**: requires no companion plugin; the only interop surface is the
  optional, read-only, semver-versioned `@gitdamnit/stranger-danger/engine` export.

## Security improvements

- **File reads never modify files.** The pre-read hook is strictly read-only; a
  detected secret no longer rewrites the file on disk.
- **Effective outbound protection.** 0.1.0's V1 `event` handler only audited
  after the fact. 0.2.0 redacts before transmission.
- **Fail-closed by construction.** Bounded, windowed scanning: content over the
  size ceiling, a window timeout/error, a cyclic structure, or nesting beyond 32
  levels is replaced with an explicit marker instead of being passed through.
- **Cycle-safe structured redaction** — fixes a fail-open where a self-referential
  tool output left the entire result, including plain string secrets, unredacted.
- **`Tool.Error.metadata` is redacted** (it is surfaced to the model).
- **No raw secrets in output.** CLI, tools, and the audit log report safe metadata
  only (rule, description, source, line/column, 8-hex fingerprint, redaction
  token). The audit log never stores the matched value.
- **Safe `sd redact`** — atomic write (temp + fsync + rename); no plaintext backup
  in the working tree unless opted in, and then a `0600` backup outside the tree.
- **Critical regex fix** — RE2/Pcre constructs that crashed `new RegExp` at import
  time are translated to valid JavaScript.
- **`sd_scan` input bounded** to 8 MiB so a model-invoked scan cannot exhaust
  memory or hang the server.
- **Directory installs load** — the package ships a root `index.js`, so
  `{ "package": "/path/to/stranger-danger" }` no longer silently fails with
  "Plugin entrypoint not found".

## Compatibility

- OpenCode **V2** runtime, `@opencode/plugin >= 2.0.0`
  (validated against `@opencode/plugin@2.0.29` on OpenCode `2.0.21`).
- Node `>= 20` (CI and runtime validation on Node 22).

## Installation

### OpenCode V2 plugin

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@gitdamnit/stranger-danger"]
}
```

> npm publication is pending (see [Distribution](#distribution)). Until then,
> install from the repository, or point `plugins` at a local checkout directory.

### Standalone CLI

```bash
npm install -g @gitdamnit/stranger-danger   # once published to npm
```

## Upgrade notes

- **Breaking:** 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 migrates to the OpenCode **V2** plugin API.
  Configure the plugin under `plugins` (not the V1 `plugin` key) and run an
  OpenCode V2 host.
- Rule count is now **236** (was ~172).
- The pre-read hook no longer rewrites files. If you relied on that behavior,
  use `sd redact` (or your own tooling) to remediate files on disk.
